title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI quality gating and metrics exporter
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: our per-prompt regression checks are useful but brittle for large prompt sets. This change adds a configurable per-prompt quality gating step to the eval-harness CI so that PRs can fail fast when a prompt's metric drops below an acceptable threshold. It also adds a lightweight metrics exporter (prometheus/textfile) so CI job results can be scraped by our observability stack for longitudinal trend analysis.

What I changed: added a new per-prompt gating runner, a metrics-exporter module, and CI workflow updates to run the gating as a required check. Included a small compatibility shim so existing eval configs continue to work.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement per-prompt gating logic with configurable thresholds
- [x] Add metrics exporter and CI integration
- [x] Update docs and example configs
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for gating behavior
- [x] Add Linear/Jira links for tracking

How it works (brief): the gating runner executes the eval-harness against the provided prompt-set and computes per-prompt metrics (e.g., exact_match, pass_at_k, quality_score). If any prompt falls below the threshold configured in .eval-ci.yml the job marks the check as failed and prints a summary table. The metrics exporter writes a textfile compatible with Prometheus node_textfile_collector so CI runners can push results to our metrics pipeline for retention and dashboards.

Backward compatibility: default behavior keeps previous global gating semantics unless the new per-prompt gating section is present in the eval config. The CI workflow falls back to the global gate if per-prompt config is absent.

Related: ENG-8241 (per-prompt gating design), SUP-4123 (customer incident triggered tighter gating for critical prompts).
